Description.Name: Bagele's Stash
Description.Details:
Darius appears on the command deck, datapad in hand and looking equal parts amused and concerned.

"Commander, remember that mysterious supply cache Bagele mentioned? The one supposedly hidden by an old client who trusted nobody and buried emergency stockpiles all over the Periphery?"

You nod.

"Well… either Bagele has an incredible imagination, or {TGT_MW.Subj} {TGT_MW.Gender?NonBinary:knew:Default:knew} exactly where to look."

The main display changes to a sensor image. A small asteroid slowly rotates through space. Tethered to its surface by heavy cables is a large supply pod. And every square meter of its hull is covered in faded hazardous material warnings.

At almost the same moment, Bagele arrives on the bridge. One look at the display and {TGT_MW.Subj} {TGT_MW.Gender?NonBinary:stop:Default:stops} dead. "No way…"

"You recognize it?" you ask.

"The markings, yes. Those warning symbols were his idea. He used to joke that nobody steals a container marked 'Dangerous Radioactive Material.' Most people won't even get close enough to read the labels."

Darius zooms in on the image. "According to our sensors, the warnings are mostly fake. Mostly. There are traces of radiation, but nothing dangerous at this distance."

You study the display again. The pod looks intact despite its appearance. The tether cables are worn but still holding.

Darius folds his arms. "The pod isn't broadcasting, and I'm not detecting any active defenses. That doesn't necessarily mean it's safe. People who hide supplies in the middle of nowhere usually don't want strangers poking around in them."

The bridge falls silent. A mysterious supply cache from Bagele's past, hidden in deep space and marked with warnings designed to keep everyone away.

Darius finally breaks the silence. "So, Commander… there's a supply pod tethered to an asteroid. It's covered in hazardous material warnings, and we have absolutely no idea what's inside." He looks up from his datapad. "Do you want to open it?"

Description.Name: Open the pod.
Description.Details: Order the pod opened

Description.Name: Send Bagele out to open the pod.
Description.Details: You look at [[TGT_MW,{TGT_MW.Callsign}]]. "What's in this pod?" Bagele frowns and leans over to check the sensor readings. "Honestly Commander, your guess is as good as mine. I never asked what my clients were hiding away and I don't plan on asking now." Darius starts to frown and begins paging through the sensor readings. "I'm not sure what to make of it, Commander. Sensors are picking up what could be an inactive fusion core or something else entirely. The pod doesn't look dangerous, but I'd recommend opening it outside. Just in case anything happens." Bagele nods in agreement. "It's probably the safest course of action. My client liked to hide stuff in the middle of nowhere for good reason. It's probably safe, but I wouldn't want to bet on it." The Argo backs off to a safe distance while the pod remains drifting alone in open space. Bagele approaches cautiously in an EVA suit as the bridge crew watches through external cameras. "No obvious damage," Bagele reports. "Power readings are low. Whatever's inside has been dormant for a long time." After several minutes of inspection, Bagele locates the primary access mechanism. "Looks like a standard security lock. Whoever hid this wasn't expecting sophisticated salvage crews." The lock releases with a metallic clunk. The pod's doors slowly unfold. Bagele's helmet camera illuminates the interior. "Commander... I think you'll want to see this." The feed zooms in. The small pod is packed with assorted hardware: Ammunition. Life Support Modules. Boosters. Darius immediately straightens in his chair. "That's not random cargo. That's a small cache." Bagele nods. "A pirate cache, by the look of it. Somebody buried a supply reserve out here." "Can you identify the owner?" you ask. "Not immediately," Bagele replies. "Most of the markings have been deliberately removed. But this is definitely pirate stock." Darius begins reviewing the inventory feed. "Not bad for a random pod floating in the middle of nowhere." The recovery crews move in as inventory scans begin, and for the first time since discovering the pod, it looks like the mystery may actually pay off.

Description.Name: Disaster
Description.Details: You look at [[TGT_MW,{TGT_MW.Callsign}]]. "What's in this pod?" Bagele frowns and leans over to check the sensor readings. "Honestly Commander, your guess is as good as mine. I never asked what my clients were hiding away and I don't plan on asking now." Darius starts to frown and begins paging through the sensor data. "I'm not sure what to make of it, Commander. Sensors are picking up what could be an inactive fusion core. The pod doesn't look dangerous, but I'd recommend opening it outside. Just in case anything happens." Bagele nods in agreement. "It's probably the safest course of action. My client liked to hide stuff in the middle of nowhere for good reason. It's probably safe, but I wouldn't want to bet on it." Several hours later, the Argo has backed away to a safe distance while the pod remains drifting alone in open space. Bagele approaches cautiously in an EVA suit while the command crew watches through external cameras. "No obvious damage," Bagele reports. "I'm seeing a standard access panel." "Proceed carefully," Darius says. Bagele moves toward the access panel and begins examining the locking mechanism. "Strange," Bagele mutters. "There's a secondary cable running through the release assembly. That's not stan—" The transmission cuts off beneath a blinding flash. The pod erupts into a violent explosion.with fragments of armor plating, shattered electronics, and molten debris scattering into space as the blast consumes the container. "BAGELE!" Darius shouts. For several terrifying seconds, the tactical display shows nothing but expanding debris. Then a contact appears. "I've got him!" one of the technicians calls out. "Suit telemetry is active! He's alive!" Relief washes across the bridge. Only briefly. The medical readouts begin streaming in. "Multiple fractures, suit penetration, burns, and concussion symptoms," the chief medic reports. "His suit absorbed most of the blast, but he's hurt badly." Darius stares at the tactical display. "The entire pod was booby-trapped. The moment the access mechanism was disturbed, it triggered a self-destruct charge." You look at the debris cloud where the pod once floated. There is nothing left to recover. Whatever the mysterious cache contained—whether valuable technology, hidden supplies, or losTech—has been completely destroyed. As recovery craft race toward Bagele's position, Darius shakes his head. "Whoever hid that pod wasn't interested in protecting its contents. They were interested in making sure nobody else ever got them."

"There's a secondary cable running through the release assembly. That's not stan—" The transmission cuts off beneath a blinding flash. The pod erupts into a violent explosion.with fragments of armor plating, shattered electronics, and molten debris scattering into space as the blast consumes the container. "BAGELE!" Darius shouts. For several terrifying seconds, the tactical display shows nothing but expanding debris. Then a contact appears. "I've got him!" one of the technicians calls out. "Suit telemetry is active! He's alive!" Relief washes across the bridge. Only briefly. The medical readouts begin streaming in. "Multiple fractures, suit penetration, burns, and concussion symptoms," the chief medic reports. "His suit absorbed most of the blast, but he's hurt badly." Darius stares at the tactical display. "The entire pod was booby-trapped. The moment the access mechanism was disturbed, it triggered a self-destruct charge." You look at the debris cloud where the pod once floated. There is nothing left to recover. Whatever the mysterious cache contained—whether valuable technology, hidden supplies, or losTech—has been completely destroyed. As recovery craft race toward Bagele's position, Darius shakes his head. "Whoever hid that pod wasn't interested in protecting its contents. They were interested in making sure nobody else ever got them."

Description.Details: You look at [[TGT_MW,{TGT_MW.Callsign}]]. "What's in this pod?" Bagele frowns and leans over to check the sensor readings. "Honestly Commander, your guess is as good as mine. I never asked what my clients were hiding away and I don't plan on asking now." Darius starts to frown and begins paging through the sensor readings. "I'm not sure what to make of it, Commander. Sensors are picking up what could be an inactive fusion core or something else entirely. The pod doesn't look dangerous, but I'd recommend opening it outside. Just in case anything happens." Bagele nods in agreement. "It's probably the safest course of action. My client liked to hide stuff in the middle of nowhere for good reason. It's probably safe, but I wouldn't want to bet on it." The Argo backs off to a safe distance while the pod remains drifting alone in open space. Bagele approaches cautiously in an EVA suit as the bridge crew watches through external cameras. "No obvious damage," Bagele reports. "Power readings are low. Whatever's inside has been dormant for a long time." After several minutes of inspection, Bagele locates the primary access mechanism. "Looks like a standard security lock. Whoever hid this wasn't expecting sophisticated salvage crews." The lock releases with a metallic clunk. The pod's doors slowly unfold. Bagele's helmet camera illuminates the interior. "Commander... I think you'll want to see this." The feed zooms in. The small pod is packed with assorted hardware: Assorted Weapons. Life Support Modules. Boosters. Darius immediately straightens in his chair. "That's not random cargo. That's a small cache." Bagele nods. "A pirate cache, by the look of it. Somebody buried a supply reserve out here." "Can you identify the owner?" you ask. "Not immediately," Bagele replies. "Most of the markings have been deliberately removed. But this is definitely pirate stock." Darius begins reviewing the inventory feed. "Not bad for a random pod floating in the middle of nowhere." The recovery crews move in as inventory scans begin, and for the first time since discovering the pod, it looks like the mystery may actually pay off.

Description.Name: Refuse to open the pod.
Description.Details:
You look at [[TGT_MW,{TGT_MW.Callsign}]]. "What's in this pod? "Bagele frowns and leans over to check the sensor readings. "Honestly Commander, your guess is as good as mine. I never asked what my clients were hiding away and I don't plan on asking now."

 Darius starts to frown and starts paging through the sensors readings, visibly agitated."Commander, you have to get us out of here now, some lunatic booby trapped this pod. Sensors are picking up a live Fusion reaction. I think some crazy bastard wired up a Fusion Core as an improvised nuke."

Bagele looks startled and alarmed."It's certainly possible, my clients were dangerous people. I only supplied the pod and the coordinates. What they did with it was never my concern." 

Bagele continues,"I certainly have no plans to end up as a smear of mildly exciting debris out in the ass end of nowhere. I didn't expect this to go bust, but I do have a consolation prize.  I'll pass along the location of my custom Hatchetman.  Let me repay you by earning my keep.  I assure you, you will not be disappointed."

You give the order to abort approach much to the crews relief.
